Mezoladany Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mezőladány, Hungary

Not demolished. Mezőladány's Jewish cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, with its newest tombstone dated 1936. The village itself formed in the 19th century from the merger of three smaller villages; its first Jews likely arrived from Galicia to trade at Kisvárda's weekly markets, later becoming tenants and eventually property owners under local nobility's patronage. The Reismann family built the area's largest lumber yard here around 1900. Jewish population peaked at 135 (over 10% of residents) in 1880, declining to 133 by 1941. In April 1944, the community's 106 Orthodox members were first confined in a local resident's stable before transfer to the Kisvárda Ghetto and deportation to Auschwitz; no survivor records exist for Mezőladány specifically, and only 6 Jews remained by 1949.
